sourceSupplements.pointerScope: Trusted browser touch events on supplied controller assets; controlled local WebSocket transport. Actual TV response is a separately labelled host fixture.
sourceSupplements.protocolScope: Controlled public native-host input snapshots with the real shared runtime and production game. Separate from trusted controller touch transport; no physical Android/LAN/phone claim.
sourceSupplements.visualGapScope: Actual ordinary browser sessions for missing original-image coverage; declared partial stops are not terminal wins. All reads are sparse.

sparseCandidateAudit.scope: Lossless selection and segmentation only. Projection time is not game time; no execution, geometry, lifecycle or independent-audit pass is asserted.
limitations: Checks public numerical projections; does not authenticate capture provenance or source-hash contents.
JSON snapshots cannot prove object identity, alias freedom, deep freezing, getter/trap behavior, or absence of hidden code.
Display message content is not a decision field; only its type/length is checked, except exact create and no-op snapshots.
Does not establish renderer visibility, actual phone contact/release, browser lifecycle, recording readability, or hardware performance.
All sparse interval continuity, unseen rotations, input edges, call dt and gate changes remain not-observed or review-required.
Embedded receipts are checked for arithmetic consistency only; no embedded history is promoted to observed adjacent transitions.
Equal endpoint poses do not exclude intervening full revolutions; endpoint call counts do not reveal individual calls.
Declared source indices, segment boundaries and parent clock metadata are preserved claims requiring source review.
Menu/null-model observations are retained but have no model endpoint to check.

preservedHistory.startupScope: Timeout before the first snapshot or screenshot. Initial page errors were not captured; this is not a recorded gameplay loss or an arithmetic-audit failure.
resolvedFindings: Atlas paint callback signature corrected before current browser generation
Decorative lower tray borders isolated behind opaque readout bands

rootLimitations: Terminal blurred scenes do not expose individual shadow cells; actual model snapshots separately audited
Sparse image brackets are not exact-frame model proof
candidatePeerLimitations: Exactly 13 current-generation files were personally opened in seven batches of at most two. Two duplicate pairs give 11 unique hashes; duplicate files are not treated as extra unique visual states.
The only active-board task shown is WEST CAST at 1280x720. The diagonal-source file is a diagonal source direction, not a task-2 screenshot.
960x540 files show blurred result modals, not the active board. Active 960x540 and tasks 1/2 remain outside this review.
No image-only claim is made about full action history, closed-edge implementation, clocks, input gates, phone touch hit areas, text-selection prevention, frame rate or hardware.
Stage blur is visible for menu, pause and outcomes; outer HUD/sidebar are not blurred. Blurred final scenes do not provide a fine-grained final-mask geometric proof.
The preserved v2 review still records its actual minor defect. Neither that review nor the earlier callback-startup failure is erased by the v3 result.
No later capture, future source generation or unopened artifact is marked reviewed.
supplementaryPeerLimitations: This is a supplementary art/layout review, not an independent re-execution of the model or a complete input-transition audit.
Result overlays intentionally blur and cover the scene; won captures support visible terminal HUD/result text and dialog appearance, not a cell-by-cell visual proof of the hidden final mask.
Sparse screenshots do not establish every intervening input, latency or frame timing. No physical phone, Android TV, production Android server, LAN performance or hardware FPS is claimed.
The separate 13 candidate-v3 originals are outside this supplementary review and are assigned to another peer. Earlier failing candidate captures remain separate preserved evidence.

Read-window timestamps only nominate nearby encoded frames, not frame-exact physics identity; no television/phone hardware or deviceFPS claim. Success modal intentionally blurs final board, so exactfinalmask comes from separate public-state audit. No visual issue identified.
limitations: These are 12 selected decoded indices and their recorded original JPEG counterparts, not a new full-video playback or a second full-validation decode. The whole clip's unselected intervals are outside this visual sample.

The manifest selects candidate indices using sparse public observation/reception-clock alignment. A selected observation is not asserted to be the exact encoded frame's physics timestamp, and names are not authoritative state labels.

Visible state values below are transcribed from the opened images. Corresponding source JPEG hashes were checked against actual files; exact source-to-encode index construction is attributed to the separate extraction manifest rather than independently rederived here.
Matching endpoints do not prove every intermediate action, continuous gate state or physical frame rate. No physical phone/TV, LAN latency, device FPS or input-edge audit is claimed.
The win dialog intentionally blurs/covers the underlying board; its visible result and HUD are reviewed, but hidden final cells are not visually reconstructed from the blurred background.
